newsitem.title: CROATIA: Workers oppose split of Croatia's post and telcoms.
newsitem.headline: Workers oppose split of Croatia's post and telcoms.

text.p: Employees of Croatia's state post and telecommunications monopoly HPT oppose its proposed split into two companies, the national daily Vjesnik reported on Monday.
It said the HPT workers' union backed up postponement of a parliamentary debate on the draft bill on HPT which includes this provision.

"Through the split...unprofitable and technologically undeveloped posts would become an additional burden for the state and its budget," said the union, voicing fears about a likely job erosion among the postal staff:
"Therefore the future of 12,000 postal workers and their families would be put into question."
The HPT union also warned that more money was constantly being invested in telecommunications, leaving the other business to "considerably lag behind in development".
Yet postal services were expected to rise some eight percent this year, Vjesnik said.
Of the total 1.3 billion kuna ($217 million) 1996 investment, almost 96 percent went into upgrading the telecommunications network and opening new land and mobile telephone lines.
HPT has not yet announced its results for 1996, after posting a net profit of 337 million kuna a year earlier.
But its development plan for this year foresees a large increase in the number of telephone users to 130,000 on the landlines and to 45,000 in the mobile network, Vjesnik said.
Splitting the two parts of the country's most profitable government-controlled company would be a first step toward its eventual privatisation sometime in the next two years.
Up to 30 percent of its 8.6 billion kuna assets may be offered to foreign investors. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075= ($ = 5.99 Croatian Kuna)
